utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers -- I'm sorry. I've got ahead. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: 219, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Major, after discussions with counsel, at the Court's direction, we're going to move through much of this material quite quickly, just so you know how we're proceeding. Is it correct sir, that on the 30th of April, 1993, you and an ECMM team also inspected an HVO prison at Kiseljak, at the Kiseljak barracks, and at that location you found that there were 48 Muslim civilian men detained in an approximately 93-cubic-metre room?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any understanding, talking to the HVO commander or based on your observations at the location, why these particular civilian men were detained?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were detained because they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine any other reason why they were being kept there at that time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that on the 8th of May, 1993, you visited Fojnica, which is southwest of Kiseljak; it was peaceful there, and the Muslims and Croats there were still living together without any problems?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 11th of May of 1993, did an RC Zenica team, including yourself, report the matter of two Muslim families in Nova Bila who were forced out of their houses by a special HVO unit, and then two Croat families were moved into the Muslim houses in their place?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were actually observing as the HVO was moving the Muslim families out and moving the Croat families in?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the commander -- did you understand the commander of this HVO unit was someone nicknamed "Zuti"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And "Zuti," to your knowledge, in Serbo-Croatian means "yellow"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Zuti was there supervising the operation?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that on the 10th of June, 1993, you were appointed chairman of a commission called the Joint Humanitarian Commission to oversee the release of prisoners pursuant to a recent ceasefire agreement which was signed by General Petkovic for the HVO and by the senior commander of the ABiH? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, sir, that one of the important features of this agreement was an agreement by both sides to release prisoners?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of then carrying out your new duties as chairman of this commission, around the 15th of June, 1993, did you hear that -- or obtain some information that Muslim prisoners were being kept at the HVO police station at the Vitez cinema?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was the Vitez cinema which, first of all, was only a few hundred metres away from Colonel Blaskic's headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was also in the very same building that Mario Cerkez's headquarters was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 15th of June, sir, based on that information, did you proceed to the HVO police station at the cinema?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you talked to the police chief?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the police chief first told you that there were no prisoners in the police station, and you responded to that by showing him a document which authorised you to search the building; and on being confronted with this authorisation, the police chief then admitted to you that there were five Muslim civilians in a small room in the basement?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were in poor condition?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these soldiers, sir, to the best of your -- based on your observations at the time?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they were civilian. One of them was too young to be a soldier and four of them were too old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. You saw these civilians, did you, in the basement?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on, on the 21st of June, 1993, did you and members of the prisoner commission go to the HVO prison at Kiseljak barracks?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived there, the HVO commander at the Kiseljak barracks told you that all of the prisoners there had already been released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You asked him for some written certification or confirmation that that was in fact the case, and upon being confronted on that, the commander changed his position and basically said, "Well, they are not released. They are working in the field"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, sir, from where you stood in having this meeting and around the Kiseljak barracks, see any fields or farms in that immediate area?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you push -- did you question the HVO commander further about his explanation that the prisoners were in the field?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Actually he told me that it was his way to say that they were on the battlefield, digging trenches and clearing mine fires -- minefields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after he told you that? What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course we made a protest at the spot and asked him to bring them back. I told him a little about the Geneva Convention, and he told me that they didn't count the Geneva Convention for anything down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, first of all -- let's take that in a little smaller pieces. First of all, on being pushed, he admitted to you himself that these prisoners, these Muslim prisoners, were out digging trenches and clearing minefields?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you protested and mentioned to him the compliance with the Geneva Conventions, his response to you was what?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That it wasn't used in this conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you waited there, and is it correct, sir, that about ten hours later the prisoners returned to camp and you saw that they were Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, one minor point of clarification. Could we know the name and rank of the individual who made these statements? I don't know that counsel has established that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, if you know that information could you give it to us?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know the name of the commander, but he was the commander of Kiseljak barracks and the person who was responsible for the prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Kiseljak for the purposes of carrying out your mission as the chairman of this commission, how did you come about identifying this person or come into contact with this person as the responsible person there?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: One of the members of this Joint Humanitarian Commission was Mr. Skopljak from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Pero Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Skopljak pointed or directed you to this HVO officer as the person in charge?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it correct, sir, that the prisoners then, once they'd returned to camp under your supervision, were released and transported to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention one last time to the photographs. It should be the last item in the bundle of photographic or map material; it is 1894.1, 1894.1. This is an aerial photograph of Kiseljak or part of Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you previously circled on this aerial photograph the Kiseljak -- a portion of the Kiseljak barracks which were being used by the HVO as a prison?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's marked there approximately to the left of the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let the record show the witness is pointing to the circled area in blue. All right. Now, these prisoners that were released, again, you were able to confirm that when they came back to the camp they were in civilian clothes, and when they were questioned through interpreters they identify themselves, in fact, as civilians?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And ICRC had interviewed them as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 23rd of June, 1993, sir, did you go to Skradno, which is east of Vitez, where you learned that the HVO was holding 88 Muslim prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to determine whether these Muslims were people who were from Skradno or is it correct, sir, that they had been brought or taken there by the Bosnian Croats from another village called Bukovci?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct. They were not from Skradno. The HVO had transported them from Bukovici to Skradno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to talk to these prisoners or some of them?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they express any particular concern to you at that time about being held in Skradno?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. They were very afraid that Skradno should be a new Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you understand they -- did they say anything to you to explain what they meant by that statement?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were afraid that the HVO will make another massacre against them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct -- turning to a different -- moving on to a different subject or topic -- that a commander in military forces is not only expected to issue orders or make his orders or wishes known to his subordinate officers, but that there's also -- he has also the responsibility to see that those orders are carried out?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your 20-plus years in the Danish army, is it correct, sir, that one of the commander's responsibilities is to make sure his subordinates know that they are to comply with the Laws and Customs of War, including the Geneva Conventions? And in the Danish army, in fact, is that part of the training that all officers receive?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: All officers and all men, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it falls to the commander to make sure that those laws and responsibilities are complied with?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could ask you to look at and direct the Court's attention to Exhibit 550.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is a last bundle of exhibits. There are actually a number of exhibits -- I haven't counted them offhand but say ten or a dozen -- that are all bound, again, in the order in which I intend to go through them, rather quickly, but the Court will see -- well, let me tell the Court what they are. No secret. These are a series of orders starting about the 17th of March and continuing until approximately the 24th of April of 1993, issued by Colonel Blaskic and others, directing the HVO troops to comply with it, essentially my shorthand term, "International Humanitarian Law," to investigate for any criminal conduct among the troops to make sure that civilians were not mistreated, to make sure that civilian property was not damaged or looted, to make sure that any alleged atrocities were investigated. You'll see that -- the Court, counsel, and the witness will see that in the course of this bundle of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Your having summarised it in that way, is it necessary to go through them?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Only briefly. I want to hit a few points in each one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take a little bit more time with the first one, 550, just to orient everyone to the rest of the bundle. Once you understand the one document, the rest are somewhat similar. On Exhibit 550, this is an order from Colonel Blaskic dated the 17th of March, titled "The Treatment of Persons Inclined to Criminal and Destructive Conduct." Now, looking over to the right top portion of the page, sir, these are apparently -- is it correct to say, as a military officer, that Colonel Blaskic is directing the orders to the units, components, listed there?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he starts with commanders of HVO brigades in his area of command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would include the Vitez Brigade commanded by Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He gave the orders to the Vitezovi special task force?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He gave the orders to the Vitez military police, 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He gave the orders to chief of Travnik police department?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he gave chief -- and he gave these orders to HVO presidents "(to be notified)"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to highlight one of the paragraphs, in paragraph number 1, it's his order -- it's -- excuse me, Colonel Blaskic's order, among other things, to immediately order platoon, company, and battalion commanders at all levels to assess the conduct of conscripts and name the persons inclined toward destructive and criminal conduct in particular. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it typical sir, that the way the -- in the military chain of command that when a superior officer issues an order, then his subordinate officers you would expect to issue orders on down the line, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to Exhibit 553, which is the next exhibit, Your Honour, after the various -- after the French translation and B/C/S translation of that document, to get to Exhibit 553. Sir, this is an order the very next day, you will see, the 18th of March 1993. If you look at the second page of that exhibit, this was an order by Mario Cerkez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you -- looking at the text of his order, Mr. Cerkez's order, you will see that, is it essentially correct, passes on, or if you want to use the word "duplicates," essentially Colonel Blaskic's order; is that correct? At least the top part?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again -- all right. Mr. Cerkez is passing it on down his chain of command, including, again, the people and groups listed on the top right portion, "Attention: HVO leadership, Attention: 1st Battalion commander," all the way down to brigade military police. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. And including the artillery commander in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, as with Colonel Blaskic, paragraph 1, he directs all of his subordinates to essentially assess and identify any perpetrators of destructive acts, especially criminal ones?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you go to Exhibit 554, --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I have to object. The evidence we just passed through alleged Cerkez order under Z553. We have only translation. Then there is another order, 554, which is signed by the battalion commander, so a level under Cerkez, and this one has the original document and translation as well. But the Cerkez order does not have -- we do not have a document. There's no document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Counsel's absolutely correct. I can provide it. For whatever reason it was not immediately with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would do so as soon as convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'll ask someone to send it over, Your Honour. My apologies. I'll check again. I checked it several times, but for some reason it was not with the document and my apologies to counsel but it will be provided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go to Exhibit 554, as counsel has just indicated, this is an order, the next day, still the next day, the 19th of March, and this is by one of Mr. Cerkez's subordinate commanders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the 1st Battalion of the Viteska Brigade. So we have in this series of orders, we have an order from Colonel Blaskic on the 17th of March, going to Mario Cerkez, Mario Cerkez's order on the 18th of March to his subordinates, and then an order on the 19th of March from one of Mr. Cerkez's subordinates to his officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to Exhibit 572, it should be the next in the bundle. This is an order from Colonel Blaskic dated the 26th of March, 1993, and essentially setting out again directed to all unit commanders in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, "Subject: Clarification on persons authorised to appoint and dismiss officers and noncommissioned officers," and according to Colonel Blaskic and the official publications of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, one might refer to it as the Narodni List or Official Gazette, he then lists at the various levels persons authorised to appoint and dismiss officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pointing your attention to, in particular, for present purposes, paragraph number 3, is it made clear, sir, that the brigade commanders, such as Mario Cerkez, had the authority to appoint and dismiss subordinate officers?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to the next exhibit, 715, this is an order by Colonel Blaskic dated the 18th of April. And in among other things, I just want to highlight paragraph 4, gather the relevant data about the actors of the conflict, the causes of banishing people, murdering civilians and soldiers, burning houses and other buildings. And Colonel Blaskic ordered all of his commanders to make those inquiries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was copied, you will see at the top, to the UNPROFOR commander, Colonel Stewart, and to the ECMM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By this time, in fact, there was some -- there had already been some outcry about the incidents around Ahmici and Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, do you recall that both Colonel Stewart and the ECMM were making demands on Mr. Blaskic at this time -- Colonel Blaskic -- to investigate these atrocities?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I see that counsel is on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, without going into the details, a couple of those documents, again, we only have translations, not the original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you give us the numbers, please, so we could --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: 572. 572 at least, because the other one issued by Blaskic, 715, seems to be issued at that time in both languages, English and Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Same commitment, Your Honour. We're inquiring now, electronically, as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, if there are any others missing, just shout out, will you, as we go through, if the originals are missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think we'll move -- 767 is just another order from Colonel Blaskic in a similar tone, the date of the 21st of April, the 22nd -- 781 is again the 22nd of April, 1993, by Colonel Blaskic. Among other things, item 1: "I strictly prohibit the torching of houses and other commercial facilities and looting in the zone of responsibility of Central Bosnia Operative Zone." 2: "Brigade and independent unit commanders must issue an order to their subordinates to make them responsible for preventing such crimes." 3: "The most stringent measures shall be taken against violators of this order pursuant to the regulation book on military discipline in HVO units." Going to Exhibit 791, order from Colonel Blaskic on the 23rd of April, 1993, some six or seven days after Ahmici, to all subordinate HVO commanders concerning the behaviour of HVO members and the level of military discipline. Colonel Blaskic says: "Because of very strong condemnation from the international community and the media campaign that is being conducted against the HVO and the Croatian people, which have extremely negative consequences for the overall reputation of the HVO and the achievements of the Croatian people globally, and in order to prevent further destructive activities and fully implement the orders of the HVO chief of staff or the main headquarters," and Colonel Blaskic gives further orders. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 804 is to a similar effect. So is Exhibit 805, treatment of the wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, we're going through these documents. We have them. Where do you intend to go with these documents in relation to the witness? What are you seeking to prove to us by going through and rereading these documents? We have them, in effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We know what they are about. You can mention them to us, but do you wish to obtain special information from the witness about these documents? Because we are coming to the end of the examination, and I think we need to save time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Absolutely. And the Court is absolutely correct, and no, I'm not going to go into any additional of these orders, other than the last two, in a few minutes. The purpose of the exercise was both to acquaint the Court with these orders and as a foundation to several follow-up questions to Major Baggesen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, as you said a few moments ago, is it correct to say that a military commander is expected and in fact required not only to issue orders but to make sure they are carried out?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the responsibility of a military commander if he finds that his orders are not being carried out?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The consequence could be that he had to replace one of his subordinate commanders. So if a commander of one of his units is not following this order, then he had to remove him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you here, sir, some questions that fit in here that may come up in other testimony. Are you familiar with the concept or term called a "forward command post"?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is a forward command post?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: A forward command post is a command post where the commander, with some of his staff, will be when an operation is going on. Example, if you are fighting and you have your troops in the field, then the commander of the unit would be in his forward command post, in the field, close to a front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your tenure in Central Bosnia, did you learn that General Bobetko of the Croatian army, the HV, had established a forward command post in Central Bosnia, at Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were told, but I haven't been in Gornji Vakuf; just passed through Gornji Vakuf. I've never been there as a monitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had that information been reported and made known to the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In terms of military police chain of command, it may be most helpful if you can have -- if the witness could be provided a piece of paper on the ELMO, Your Honour, because I think he can diagram an answer to my question the way he showed it to me, and it would be the most helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, if you could, if you could show a box at the brigade -- at a brigade level of what you would expect -- what the command structure would be like in terms of -- would there be a unit under the brigade level for military police?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In a NATO army, per se, the military police normally started at the corps level. At the corps level, there's normally a military police battalion. At brigade level, there's normally one military police company, or corps, and this military police unit is coming from this unit [indicates]. But the commander of this brigade has a military police company in operational control. From the brigade, the brigade commander is able to take one platoon from this military police company and put it down to the battalion level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you've shown us on this chart -- and we'll mark this as an exhibit, Your Honour -- you've shown us from the level of the corps -- from the corps -- from the level of the corps to the brigade to the battalion, but focusing on that -- I'm sorry, yes, you can leave it on for a moment -- what is now essentially the middle of the page, the military police unit would be assigned at the brigade level, and for day-to-day operational control, who would control that military -- who would control that military police unit?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps, on the exhibit, if I could just suggest, could you draw perhaps some other dotted line from the brigade command, what would be indicative of the brigade commander to that military police unit?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes [indicates]. Okay?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where are we on the outline, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're between 237 and 238. It's my mistake for not having updated the outline. But that's it, Your Honour. We're now going to 238.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is the structure as put forward by the Major, is that a universal structure, in military --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That was my next -- I guess 238 was the next -- Mr. President, that was my next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've indicated, Major, that this would be the common structure in a NATO army. Based on your experience in having analysed the Warsaw Pact forces for many years and on any experience or training you observed in Central Bosnia, do you know whether that structure, or something very similar to it, applied to the HVO forces?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The structure was similar in the Warsaw Pact and in the Soviet Bloc, and it was similar in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So at least as to the JNA doctrine and practice, that would have been the structure, to best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, if you're going to move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- away from that exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- we must get it marked. And perhaps, Major, if you could write on the top of it, so we have it for future reference, something to the effect of "NATO Military Police Structure," if that's right.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would do that, and then sign it "Major Baggesen", and then we will remember in the months to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, our case manager indicates that we can't assign it a number at the moment, but we promise to, at the first opportune moment, inform the Court and registrar what the number is in our list, existing list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, you have shown us a certain number of documents, and if I understand well, regarding the orders issued by Colonel Blaskic, concerning offences and behaviour contrary to international law, committed at lower levels, we have seen this diagram shown to us regarding the position of the military police in the hierarchy. Does that mean that these orders did not go right down to the bottom? That is a question that we could ask the witness. Does the witness know what happened with these orders that you have just quoted from in detail, and which have been confirmed to have been issued by Colonel Blaskic? Therefore does he know what happened to these orders that were issued? Were they implemented to the best knowledge of the witness, or were they intentionally ignored? What happened to these orders, if the witness knows?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, when we visited the subunits, we didn't know anything about these orders. We asked them because we knew that Colonel Blaskic had made some orders and normally when we are -- we were visiting the different headquarters, we asked them if they had received orders to do this and this and this. And on the other side, we didn't see any proof that any soldiers who have been responsible for looting or burning houses had been punished. So he made the orders, as he should do as a commander, but if he sent them to his units or he put them into a drawer, we don't know. We have not seen the orders at the lower level commands. So I cannot -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is a mistake in the transcript, I see. At the beginning of the Major's answer, it reads "when we visited the subunits, we didn't know anything about these orders." Is that what you said, Major?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: They.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's what I thought you said, "They didn't know about the orders." Yes. That's a crucial difference.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, we saw that the Viteska Brigade commander, Mr. Cerkez, had the order and he gave an order to his battalion level, but we haven't seen anything from other units. The commander in Kiseljak, he didn't know about this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you're giving us some additional information in relation to your previous statement. You said Commander Cerkez did receive orders from Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were able to verify that Mr. Cerkez, as a brigade commander, had indeed received orders from Colonel Blaskic. They were transmitted to him. But you didn't see, at the level of lower units, that they were passed on after that.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have only seen the surface orders here in court just before, one of these. That's what I was trying to say. I have only seen this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The Exhibit 553.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Dated the 18th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, except for this document, that is, the Exhibit 553, you yourself, when you went out into the field, you never saw any trace of Colonel Blaskic's orders at the level of various units in the field. You never saw those orders because when on the ground, they didn't tell you about General Blaskic's orders to put an end to offensive and criminal behaviour that has been noted by you over there. Am I correct in understanding you?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just to finish on that before moving on then, Major. It's your testimony that by -- in the few days following the events in Ahmici on the 16th of April --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I have that question again, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I was just waiting on the Court. It's your testimony that by -- or during the first few days following the events in Ahmici on the 16th of April, by that time there was known to be an international outcry about the alleged atrocities in Ahmici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was generally known -- in fact, some of the orders that Colonel Blaskic was sending, copies of his orders to the ECMM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he had, thereafter, at least on paper, made a number of orders?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those you did know or the ECMM did know that those orders existed?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew that he had issued orders after Ahmici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, you had been on the Busovaca Joint Commission when you first arrived in April of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is it correct that the Busovaca Joint Commission was established in January 1993 and continued for approximately five months into approximately the latter part of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were a member of the Busovaca Joint Commission, would it be fair to say that both yourself and other members of ECMM made a number of complaints on a regular basis about the conduct of HVO units and soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The usual HVO representative at these commission meetings was Colonel Blaskic's deputy, Franjo Nakic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you were no longer personally involved in the Busovaca Joint Commission, is it your understanding, from your colleagues, that the ECMM continued to protest and make complaints about HVO conduct at Busovaca Joint Commission meetings?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, in the commission that they were placed, the Busovaca Joint Commission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Joint Operation Commission, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During -- at any time during your tour in Central Bosnia, after these complaints were made, did any information come to your attention that any HVO unit or soldier had been disciplined or punished in connection with any of these -- any of this misconduct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, did you learn, during your time in Bosnia, that there was an instance, in fact, where one HVO Brigade commander was relieved of duty?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. There was one brigade or battalion commander that was replaced by Colonel Blaskic because this commander refused to attack a civilian village, civilian Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your recollection, is it correct sir, that that HVO Brigade commander's name was Stjepan Tuka?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention and the Court's attention to Exhibit 731.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: These are the last two exhibits, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order from Colonel Blaskic dated the 19th of April, 1993, to the commander of Fojnica battalion personally, and I may have misspoke if I said "brigade commander," but this HVO commander, directing him, or Colonel Blaskic says: "I call to your attention your duty to execute and comply with the orders issued by the commander of the Kiseljak Ban Jelacic Brigade." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Otherwise you will be replaced and will be held responsible in compliance with the regulations of Herceg-Bosna in line with military discipline." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To go on to Exhibit 743, the last in this bundle. This is a further order dated the 20th of April, 1993, by Colonel Blaskic, as indicated in paragraph -- well, to the commanders of the brigades, the Busovaca Brigade, and to the Fojnica Brigade or Battalion, and Colonel Blaskic says: "I hereby dismiss Mr. Stjepan Tuka from the post of commander of the 3rd Battalion of the --" which was the Busovaca Brigade. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This incident or this set of events was known to you and to ECMM in the spring of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your understanding was the reason that Mr. Tuka was relieved of command is because he refused to attack Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any other order or situation of any HVO officer being disciplined during your tour of duty in Central Bosnia other than Stjepan Tuka?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, if I understood well your question to the witness, Mr. Tuka -- Commander Tuka was dismissed because he refused to attack Muslim civilians. Was that the question you put to the witness? How does the witness know that? Did the witness see a document or how does he know the reason for Mr. Tuka's dismissal?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say, Major?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We were told not by Mr. Tuka, but another team were going to have a meeting in the Kiseljak area, and they were going to have a meeting with Mr. Tuka. They were told that he was not present any more because he was replaced, and he was replaced because he didn't want to -- I can't remember if it was Fojnica, but he was replaced because he refused to attack a Muslim village. So it had been told to one of our teams by members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So somebody in your team told you that he heard it from somebody from the HVO, but you cannot tell us the names of the people concerned?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not who specifically from the HVO told it to one of our team, but they were going to have a meeting with Mr. Tuka, and when they came to his headquarters, the team was told that he was replaced because he didn't want to carry out this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But who among your team in the ECMM -- who is the person who told you about this? Could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot recall which team were in Kiseljak at that time or who was a member of the team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In any event, apart from this information that you received through an intermediary, you have no other information to corroborate this report regarding the motives which led to the dismissal of Mr. Tuka? You have no other evidence except this?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. But there may be other evidence, because I can remember that it was discussed with the UNPROFOR unit in Kiseljak. So maybe they have some other evidence on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, do you have any other evidence that you'll call about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have other evidence. I think we have exhausted this particular witness's knowledge, but I think I can represent to the Court that there's other witness and documentary evidence concerning this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, just one further point of military command. Sir, in your -- based on your training experience, in a situation where the physical geography of a command might be physically disconnected, if you will, and his area might be divided in some fashion, does that any way relieve or excuse him from meeting his command obligations?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your training and experience, not only in the Danish army but your knowledge of NATO armies and the Warsaw Pact armies, do the military commanders ultimately report to their political superiors?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's normal, yes, on the higher level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your experience, sir, have you ever known of a Colonel being promoted to General who had not -- who did not -- had not carried out the wishes of his political masters?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we need an answer on that. It will be for us to draw conclusions in respect to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened -- let me ask you this question, sir: What are the ramifications for a military officer if he is known among his colleagues and among his superiors for not -- if I can repeat. What are the ramifications for a military officer if he is known among his colleagues or superiors as not being able to control his subordinates or troops?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Then he will not be promoted to a higher rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be viewed as a serious deficiency for an officer, would it not?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, sir, was your work as an ECMM monitor fully respected and subject to commendation by the ECMM and your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following your tenure as an ECMM monitor in Bosnia, is it correct, sir, that you in fact, trained new monitors for the ECMM for the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1996, sir, were you asked by the Danish Centre for Human Rights to train Russian civilian human rights monitors for service in Chechnya?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can now give some further clarification for sitting down on exhibits. The drawing that mister -- excuse me, Major Baggesen did can be marked as 2768, 2-7-6-8, and I do have the Serbo-Croatian translations for Exhibit 572 and 553, with apologies to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps someone could pass that across.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Usher, if you could pass the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, but I'm now not sure. We were not asking for Serbo-Croatian translation of the document, we were asking for the original document which is supposed to be issued in the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I think this ought to be further clarified then. Did I say -- the orders are the original or copies of the original. I didn't mean translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can the matter be clarified perhaps during the adjournment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would think so, Your Honour. It was my mistake. I should not have used the word "translation." They are the B/C/S originals of the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just in order to clear that, there are also two other documents used. It is Z767 and Z805, where copies of the original Croatian language documents are not legible at all. It's not that, you know, you can recognise a part of it, none, nothing, zero.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll attempt to address the matter further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, if you'd like to make a start, and when you find a convenient moment, about 11.00, we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have tried to put together a list of or a bunch of documents that I will try to go through sequentially with the witness. I've tried to make sure that the exhibits are all arranged in chronological order, and I hope it will facilitate an expeditious handling of the cross-examination. With the Court's permission, I'd like to hand those up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have copies for the booths, please? Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being attended to, Major, good morning. My name is Stephen Sayers. I represent Dario Kordic. Major, you've demonstrated an ability to answer in terse military language yes or no to questions, and that has facilitated the prompt handling of your direct-examination. I'd like to use the same technique in the not unrealistic hope, I hope, that we will be through with you by the end of the day. Is that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you need to say more than yes or no to questions, please let me know and we'll have the explanation given to the Trial Chamber. You were asked questions about the diagram that you drew, Exhibit Z2768, the chain of command of the military police. As I understand it, sir, you are of the opinion that the military police commanders exercised at corps level?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That detachments of the military police are then seconded essentially to battalion level; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then from battalion level down to brigade level; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, to company level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To company level. Very well. That's not unusual in military organisations, is it? In fact, that's the structure of the military police command that you observed in the HVO during your time in Central Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Actually, we were not sure if they were using the same structure as what's known from the JNA and from other armies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sure about what the military police command in the Muslim forces was, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that complaints about HVO conduct were relatively routine at the Busovaca Joint Commission meetings and at the organisation that followed that, the joint operations command. The same is true of conduct of the Muslim forces, is it not?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you do not speak any Croatian, do you?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You relied upon interpreters?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Blaskic case, you informed the Court that you had been instructed that you were not permitted to converse or speak with Defence lawyers; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Not ordered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Instructed?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It was up to ourselves if you want to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not converse with the Defence lawyers in the Blaskic case, did you?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because they already had my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same is true in this case, is it?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you kept a contemporaneous document called a "War Diary"; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was a personal diary I kept for myself. It was not -- it should not be an official document. If I had known it would be an official document, I would have maybe used some other words. So it was just a private diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would like to have a copy of this marked as the next exhibit. This is a copy of the Major's war diary, Your Honour, and I do not believe that there are any personal details in here that would be embarrassing to the Major. The entries pretty much are consumed solely with his observations during his time in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's consistent with your recollection, is it?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Some of my observations and some of my personal -- what I have are feelings about what happened down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be Exhibit D75/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You actually provided an edited version to the Prosecution of this diary, did you not?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Actually, I don't know how the Prosecutor's office had a copy of my diary. It may have been given to them by one of the other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it maintained by you in handwriting, or did you type it up?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the beginning, in Bosnia, it was handwriting. When I came back, when I had to work all my -- work it all through, I typed it on my computer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Danish. And then this had been translated from the Croatian translation of the Danish original, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The diary covers March the 30th until July the 1st, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a large block from April the 6th to April the 18th which was not maintained contemporaneously; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a summary of your observations during that time period?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, because I didn't have time enough to write the diary at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So would it be fair to say that in this contemporaneous document, you noted down significant events, significant meetings, and significant personages that you came into contact with during your ten weeks, I believe, in Central Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Some of it. Some of it. Not everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you would agree with me that there is not a single mention of Mr. Kordic's name anywhere in that contemporaneous chronicle of significant events, significant meetings, and significant persons; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think maybe he is mentioned once or twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure, if he is, that will be pointed out to you. Now, you testified for three days in the Blaskic case in 1997; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've give a statement over the course of two days in August of 1996 to the investigators for the Prosecution; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend with the Prosecutors going over your testimony over the last -- that you've given over the last two days, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I arrived this Monday, and I had a meeting, I think Tuesday, with the Prosecutor's office. And then I have been waiting for coming in court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand it, you were actually in Central Bosnia from April the 2nd to June the 28th, 1993. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. With a holiday back in Denmark from May the 19th to June the 1st of 1993?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So ten weeks is the total time that you spent in Central Bosnia, sir?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Isn't it true, sir, that it was completely normal for you to see burned houses in every village in Central Bosnia when you were there?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true also that in your personal view, essentially the legal institutions had broken down completely? The central government wasn't functioning in any realistic way, was it?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. [Indiscernible] ... work in the military way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The civil police, in your opinion, were virtually ineffective, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: People were getting robbed or shot routinely, weren't they, on both sides?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Both sides, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, you found the area embroiled in a general state of social, ethnic, and political anarchy and chaos, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, sir, it was absolutely routine and standard for both sides to try to pin the blame for events or incidents upon each other; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. And that was our job too, to do the fact-finding, to see -- to find the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But it was a standard explanation from both sides, when confronted with a particular unpleasant event, that there were uncontrolled elements within the armed forces that were responsible for that; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were known using that excuse, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you actually received a briefing in connection with your duties as a European Community Monitoring Mission monitor; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were briefed that the commander of the 3rd Corps in Zenica was General Enver Hadzihasanovic; right?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you met him a number of times?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At his headquarters in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His opposite number, you were briefed, on the HVO side, was Colonel Tihomir Blaskic; right?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You met Colonel Blaskic, I believe, about 10 or 15 times during your sojourn in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were briefed, I believe you testified, that the main Bosnian Croat political leader was Mr. Kordic. Could you just let the Trial Chamber know who you were briefed was the main Muslim political leader in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can remember that the -- we were discussing matters concerning Muslims in Central Bosnia. We were discussing it with the vice-president -- I cannot remember his name just now. I know his name, but I cannot remember it, sitting here. Maybe you can help me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you do, you do, and if you don't, you don't. Were you briefed who the Muslim political leader in Central Bosnia was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the first question is, was he briefed that there was such a political leader?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You were? But you don't remember his name?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also briefed, I believe, sir, and if you turn to the ECMM briefing document which has been marked Z495, and it's dated February the 25th in the chronological package that I've given to you, just turn to the document that is dated February the 25th, 1993. If you would turn to page 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts are we in the bundle, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There is a series of documents, Your Honour, which are arranged chronologically. They've all been separately stapled, and I'm referring to the ECMM briefing summary. If you just undo the bundle, you will see it, for February the 25th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is it the third, "Introduction Brief for New ECM Mission Monitors," number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically I would like to address your attention to page 6 of this document. Is it true that you were briefed that the army commanded by General Sefer Halilovic was 50.000 to 60.000 strong?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told in your briefing that the army had become much more organised and better equipped during the past six months?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when I refer to "the army," of course, I'm referring to the forces under the command of General Sefer Halilovic, the ABiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you instructed that the military organisation of the ABiH was that they had been divided -- the forces had been divided into five separate corps, with the 3rd Corps headquartered in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were also instructed that there was a new formation of the Muslim forces army which accepts on Islamic soldiers from Bosnia and abroad and was assessed at about 2.000 strong; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you understand that the Croats constituted a minority of about 17 per cent to 18 per cent of the total population of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Say again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand that the Croats only constituted about 17 to 18 per cent of the total population in Bosnia-Herzegovina? I'm not asking questions about that document --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Indiscernible] I'm sorry. That confused me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all right. My fault.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot remember the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it your understanding, however, that the Bosnian Croats were in a significant minority by comparison to the overall population of the country?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was not? All right. Would it be fair to say --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sorry, not in the specific area where I was working. Are you speaking of the whole of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Then you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, would it be fair to say that you were shot at fairly frequently by both sides?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it was extremely dangerous to move around or to try to move around from one locality to another, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your work in the Joint Humanitarian Commission which you've described, isn't it true that one of your colleagues, Mr. Zarko Malenica, was shot to death by a sniper as he was travelling from Busovaca to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He and a colleague went into an ambush, and they were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ambushed by Muslim forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: We don't know, but they were ambushed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Malenica and his colleague, Mr. Mravak?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And people being shot to death by snipers on both sides, unfortunately, was simply a fact of life in Central Bosnia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to your time in Vitez, it would be fair to say, sir, that you were actually based in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And throughout your time there, that was a Muslim-dominated city, controlled --

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in fact, isn't it true to say that the HVO military forces in Zenica were expunged on April the 18th, and that the headquarters of the Jure Francetic Brigade was basically captured by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it, sir, you spent a grand total of five to six nights in Vitez during your ten-week tour in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of those nights just happened to be a night that's of considerable interest to the Trial Chamber, the night of April 15th to the 16th. Just a few questions on your knowledge of Bosnian Croat political institutions, and if you don't know, just tell me, and I'll move on quickly. Do you know what the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have -- it's difficult for me to remember, because there was a lot of change [indiscernible] the government. I cannot recall it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. At the time that you were present in Central Bosnia, we've seen several documents that make a reference to the president of the HVO, Dr. Jadranko Prlic, one of them being Exhibit Z757, and I would just like you to turn to that, if you would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is one of the Prosecution exhibits, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, it is indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: 757, and I am specifically referring to page 3.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't have the document here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have the document: 757, Z757.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Major. If you would just turn to the third page. The station chief, Mr. Andersen, refers to a meeting between the ECMM and a Dr. Ganic, who is the vice-president of Bosnia-Herzegovina, along with Dr. Prlic, who is the HVO president, and apparently this resulted in an agreement at the political level?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Mr. Prlic, or Dr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to him on the telephone?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know anything about him at all?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. If you take a look at the bottom of page 2 and the top of page 3, there's a reference to a meeting which had been interrupted by an HVO Minister of Defence claiming that a large-scale ABiH offensive was on the way on the 18th of April, I believe. Do you know who that gentleman might have been, the HVO Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I was not present at the meeting, and I can't remember all the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber whether or not Mr. Kordic ever held a position in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Major, that is a question -- this isn't a memory test.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So if you can't remember, just say so, or if you simply don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can remember that during his own presentation to me, I was told that he was a vice-president of the HDZ. I can remember that he mentioned that he had some other -- what would you call it -- jobs as well. We knew that he was a political leader in Central Bosnia, and that -- I think his superior was Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn of the existence of the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Bozo Rajic?

utterances.speaker: LARS BAGGESEN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot recall the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The Trial Chamber has heard some evidence about an order that was supposedly issued by this gentleman obliging the ABiH forces in Croat-designated cantons under the Vance-Owen Plan to submit themselves to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness might be shown Prosecution Exhibit 390,2, which was Brigadier General Cordy-Simpson's document, for the Court's information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in, Major, are the two attachments to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You'll be shown it, Major. 390.2; it's a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, I'm afraid it's not in -- or maybe it is -- oh, it is, yes; I'm sorry. The date of it is January the 24th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could we find out what documents the witness has? This is a Prosecution Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- 390.2, and I would guess the Registrar has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
